info.title: Sun Tech WCS: the WMS contract
info.description:
The routes a WMS (or an adapter in front of it) serves for the WCS, generated by tools/Wcs.ContractCheck from `IWarehouse` and the real client `HttpWarehouse` (do not edit by hand). `info.version` is `WarehouseContract.Version` (WCS/Wcs.Wms.Contracts): its major part changes on a change an existing WMS would not survive.

On the wire:
- Request bodies come in two casings, written by two serializers of the client: `x-wcs-request-casing` says which per operation (PascalCase for the POSTs that read an answer body, camelCase for those whose answer body is ignored). Read property names case-insensitively. Answers are read case-insensitively, and numbers in answers may also be strings.
- Identifiers of load units, cells, areas, warehouses and rows are .NET `decimal` (`format: decimal`): the same id may come as `5001` or `5001.0`, in bodies and in path segments. Parse them as numbers, never compare them as text. Mission ids and operation ids are GUID strings. Enumerations are numbers (`enum` and `x-enum-varnames`).
- Answers: any 2xx with the expected body is used. A 404 is "there is none" only where the operation has a `404` answer (`x-wcs-not-found: none`); anywhere else it is a failure. Every 4xx except 408 and 429 is a permanent refusal: answer it only for a request that can never succeed. 5xx, 408, 429, a timeout, a dropped connection, a body that does not read and a `null` body are temporary failures: the WCS leaves the work waiting and asks again, or retries from a durable queue.
- The operations with an `OperationId` in the body (`x-wcs-operation-id: true`) are delivered at least once: keep a receipt per `OperationId`. Same id and same content (same values: `5005` and `5005.0` are the same id): answer what you answered the first time without applying it again. Same id, different content: 409. The empty GUID is not from a queue: no receipt.
- `x-wcs-durable-queue` names the table of the WCS's database (`wcs.db`) the operation is sent from.

The answer body is not read. Sent from the durable queue when the load unit has moved on the field (at least once, retried 2 s, 4 s, 6 s ... up to 30 s, in every engine state). A permanent refusal (4xx) parks the row, which holds back the later facts about the same load unit until a person resolves it. Also sent directly, with `OperationId` = the empty GUID and no receipt, when a load unit arrives on a device linked to a cell.

4XX.description: A permanent refusal (every 4xx except 408 and 429): answer it only for a request that can never succeed. The WCS logs it and does not read the body; a durable queue parks the row.

5XX.description: A temporary failure, like 408, 429, a timeout or a dropped connection: the WCS leaves the work waiting and asks again, or retries from its durable queue.

post.description: `IWarehouse.ReleaseStorageReservationAsync`. The body is written in camelCase (`{"loadUnitId":5001}`); read its names case-insensitively. A 404 is a failure like any other unexpected status. The answer body is not read. The reservations of missions closed while the engine reloaded are kept and released once at the next Run; a failure leaves them to the WMS's own expiry.
